events.title: Marriage to widow Maria Magdalena (Grub) Ihrig
events.description: Her first husband Johannes Ihrig died 1788; her 1801 St. John's Lutheran death entry names her as wife of Johann G. Stecher, previously wife of Johann Ihrig, née Grub. [R4-S1]

bio: Johann Georg Stecher, known in English records as George Stacher or Stecher, married Maria Magdalena Grub (1759–1801), the widow of Johannes Ihrig, who had died in 1788. Andreas Grub's will of 1791 calls her 'Mary the wife of George Stacher', and her death entry of 1801 at St. John's Lutheran Church in Easton names both her husbands and her maiden name. In 1790 George's household in Forks Township, Northampton County, Pennsylvania, held three males over sixteen and ten females, possibly including the aged Andreas Grub. The Stechers also married into the Doll family, since a Christopher Stecher is said to have married Elizabeth Doll, so the Grub, Stecher and Doll families moved in overlapping circles in Forks Township.

researchNotes: Johann Georg Stecher married Maria Magdalena Grub (b. 6 May 1759, d. 27 Dec 1801), widow of Johannes Ihrig (d. 1788), after 1788. Andreas Grub's 1791 will calls her 'Mary the wife of George Stacher', and her 1801 death entry at St. John's Lutheran, Easton, names both husbands and her maiden name ([R4-S1]). In 1790 George Stecher's Forks Township household had three males over 16 and ten females, possibly including the aged Andreas Grub ([R4-S1]). The Stechers also married into the Doll family (Christopher Stecher, said to have married Elizabeth Doll), which points to overlapping Grub-Stecher-Doll circles in Forks Township.
summary: Johann Georg Stecher of Forks Township, Northampton County, who married Maria Magdalena Grub, widow of Johannes Ihrig, after 1788.
